title: Dispatch: fix leftmost-open-paren semantics in stripTrailingParenthetical (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch bead for `eshyra-e1kt` (read that bead for the spec). Attempt 3 —
blocking review finding on PR #523 at head b0ff8ddf. Attempts 1 and 2 stay
merged; this repairs one defect in `stripTrailingParenthetical`.

Branch/worktree: `eshyra-e1kt.3`, cut from branch `eshyra-e1kt` (head b0ff8dd).
Model config: gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium.

## The defect

`stripTrailingParenthetical` in
`packages/core/src/state/nameNormalization.ts` claims exact equivalence to
`text.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`. It is not equivalent. It selects the
opening parenthesis with `text.lastIndexOf('(', end - 1)` — the LATEST `(` —
but the regex is leftmost-match and `[^)]*` admits `(`, so the regex can start
at an EARLIER `(`.

Confirmed counterexamples (regex result vs current helper):

| input | `/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/` | current helper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"(()"` | `""` | `"("` |
| `"name ((x)"` | `"name"` | `"name ("` |
| `"a ((b)"` | `"a"` | `"a ("` |
| `"x (( )"` | `"x"` | `"x ("` |
| `"  ((a)  "` | `""` | `"  ("` |

The attempt-1 spec asserted a false lemma — "leftmost-match forces the `(` to
be the last `(` in the string" — and the helper's doc comment and the PR body
both repeat it. The existing `'nested (a (b) c)'` fixture does not catch this
because that input has an interior `)` that makes BOTH candidate opens fail, so
the two implementations agree by accident.

## Correct semantics

The closing paren is pinned: `text[end-1]` must be `)` where
`end = text.trimEnd().length`, because `\s*$` cannot span a non-whitespace
character. So the match is `[q, end)` for an opening paren at `q` where
`text[q] === '('` and `(q, end-1)` contains no `)`.

Let `lastClose` be the index of the last `)` strictly before `end-1`. Then
`q` is viable exactly when `q > lastClose`: any `q < lastClose` puts that `)`
inside the span. The regex takes the leftmost viable `q` — and since a smaller
`q` also yields a smaller match start once the leading `\s*` run is absorbed,
leftmost `q` is leftmost match.

So the selection is `indexOf('(', lastClose + 1)`, NOT `lastIndexOf`:

```ts
export function stripTrailingParenthetical(text: string): string {
  const end = text.trimEnd().length;
  if (end === 0 || text[end - 1] !== ')') return text;
  const lastClose = end >= 2 ? text.lastIndexOf(')', end - 2) : -1;
  const open = text.indexOf('(', lastClose + 1);
  if (open === -1 || open >= end - 1) return text;
  return text.slice(0, open).trimEnd();
}
```

This is still linear: two bounded scans plus a slice, no backtracking. Verified
equivalent to the regex across all 22 inputs in the table below.

Rewrite the doc comment so it states the ACTUAL rule — leftmost `(` after the
last interior `)` — and drop the false "last `(` in the string" claim.
